messages:
sara: Hey team — Acme is hitting a surge this morning and their Dedicated pool is returning intermittent 429s. They say the reserved pool refill rate seems slower than expected and latency is creeping. SLA alarm fired. Can someone triage?
kevin: Can you paste the customer id and region? Also any request patterns (streamed vs non-streamed)?
sara: Customer: acme-corp, region: eu-west-1. Pattern: lots of short generate calls, bursty every 30s from a batch job. Mostly non-streamed but some chat streams. Seeing 429s spike from 08:12->08:20 UTC.
lina: I'm checking the billing/credits surface to ensure they haven't hit a billing block, but dashboard shows reserved pool active. No invoice issues.
raj: I'll pull token-bucket telemetry. Initial guess: refill window misaligned with their burst pattern + headroom too tight. Sending a short query to infra logs...
ops-bot: [alert] dedicated-pool-acme-corp eu-west-1 quota-exhaust at 2026-03-17T08:13:02Z — 429 rate increased by 120%
kevin: Can we repro locally against their workload? If it's short non-streamed calls, try a replay with same qps spikes. Share the replay script.
sara: Pasting a minimal repro command they used:
```
for i in {1..300}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDCRED" -d '{"model":"rwd-large", "prompt":"x"}'; sleep 0.1; done
```
They run that from 6 parallel workers.
lina: I looked at their reserved pool config — commit 6k TUs/min with burst_headroom=10%. That headroom is tight for 6-worker spikes. Might be hitting headroom floor.
raj: Telemetry: refill events are on schedule, but token consumption has high jitter. There's a penalty window kicking in on some hosts when bursts exceed configured smoothing. That causes slower replenish for ~30s.
kevin: Two actions: 1) Temp bump their reserved pool burst_headroom to 25% for today to prevent repeated 429s. 2) Add a smoothing rule to accept short microbursts (<=5s) without activating penalty. Anyone object?
sara: Customer asked for immediate mitigation — please do the temp bump. I'll tell them we're applying a short-term config change.
lina: Done — increased burst_headroom to 25% for acme-corp in eu-west-1 (audit id: audit-3301234567).
ops-bot: [config-change] user=lina changed reservedpool.burst_headroom from 10% to 25% for acme-corp eu-west-1 at 2026-03-17T08:25:12Z
raj: After bump, 429 rate dropped to baseline within one refilling cycle. Latency improved ~18ms p50. Still seeing a couple of straggler 429s tied to specific hosts. I'll pin those hosts for an extra refill pass.
kevin: For long-term: recommend increasing commit or adding a short-burst allowance policy, and advise customer to exponential backoff jitter on client side. Also consider moving heavy batch job to dedicated scheduled slot to smooth traffic.
sara: I'll send Acme the mitigation summary and next steps. Also scheduling a call to review pooling config and billing impact of temporary headroom bump.
lina: I'll track billing note — temporary bump will increase unit consumption; alerting customer.
kevin: Ticket update: assign to eng-infra for follow-up on penalty-window behavior and to product for an options doc on burst policies. Tagging @raj.
raj: On it — I'll open a short repro with exact worker counts and include host-level logs.
sara: Thanks all. Closing initial escalation but leaving ticket open until infra fix is in. :thumbsup:
